name: MrOS lateral spine radiographs (Osteoporotic Fractures in Men)
what: lateral thoracic and lumbar films of 5,994 men at six US centres, two visits (2000-2002 and about 4.6 years later), with Genant semi-quantitative vertebral fracture grades per vertebra; one deep-learning study used 4,461 subjects and 15,524 films; the image counts and the request steps to confirm on the page
level_truth: Genant grades on named levels, so level truth exists
licence: a MrOS data request agreement; terms to confirm on the page
how_to_get: Open https://mrosonline.ucsf.edu/ and read the data request route (an online application with a proposal), to confirm on the page.
The owner files the request in the owner's name and signs whatever agreement follows; a session drafts the proposal text once the owner asks.
Once granted, fetch by the route the centre gives, as a Slurm job on the owner's word, never on the login node; no fetch helper applies until the route is known.
source_status: found by the sweep of 2026-10-21; not fetched; a research data request through the MrOS coordinating centre (an online application with a proposal), not sent; the images are not on dbGaP, whose phs000373 covers genotypes (to confirm on the page); older osteoporotic spines with compression fractures, the anatomy the C-arm sees in kyphoplasty

owner's sitting prepared: MrOS Online registration is gated by an authorization email from an institutional address to mrosdata@ucsf.edu with full name and every institutional affiliation, foreign ones included; the form then asks Email, Password, First Name, Middle Initial, Last Name, Institution, Position and a box accepting the limited data set agreement (mrosonline.ucsf.edu/Account/UserAgreement, accepted by the recipient alone, no institutional signature, citation under the MrOS publication guidelines); the authorization email is drafted in the owner's Outlook Drafts; whether the spine film images are on the website or need the NIA Aging Research Biobank's Request for Materials (protocol, IRB letter, attestation, CV, then an agreement the institution's signing official signs) is asked in that email

the MrOS coordinating centre answered the owner's email: MrOS Online is closed to registrations while it is updated for new NIH requirements and will write when it reopens; the study images are being added to the NIA Aging Research Biobank (https://agingresearchbiobank.nia.nih.gov), which already holds them, so the images are requested from the Biobank, which gives the timeline, transfer, any fees and the terms of use

obstacles: MrOS Online is closed to registrations until it is updated for new NIH requirements
the images are requested from the NIA Aging Research Biobank, a request in the owner's name whose terms and any fee are his to accept
next: the owner submits a request for the MrOS lateral spine images through the NIA Aging Research Biobank (https://agingresearchbiobank.nia.nih.gov), which gives the timeline, transfer, fees and terms; MrOS Online's reopening is a second route
